cohort: The study included 422 live-born neonates from a hospital in Mekelle, Ethiopia.
finding: Chest circumference and head circumference were found to be better surrogate measurements for identifying low birth weight neonates than foot length, with chest circumference showing the highest correlation and head circumference having the highest predictive value.
birth_weight: neonates including those with low birth weight (< 2500 g)
